new_statements.relation_note: new: nothing on record (in_catalog false, no catalog record, no existing statement). First token-level evidence pointing to penultimate stress with lexical final-stress exceptions; compatible with the areal penultimate pattern Schapper & Zobel 2024:570 report for southern Maluku (a work that does not name West Masela) and with Zobel 2018's 'stressed (= penultimate) position' for Proto Southwest Maluku. Not a prose statement; confidence low.
new_statements.translation_language: IPA transcriptions of West Marsela forms against Indonesian prompts
new_statements.rule_in_words: The work states no rule (field transcription sheets; the 'notes on transcription' box is empty). The transcriber's IPA primary-stress marks, where written, fall on the penultimate syllable in the large majority of polysyllabic forms in the pages read (roughly 40 of some 50 marked forms I examined on Lawawang pp.3-6, Nura p.1, Babyotan p.2), with a lexical minority of final-stressed forms (e.g. kɛkɛkˈɲɛy 'plain', ɔnˈpɛy 'horn', βaˈbɔr(ɛ) 'wild pig', nɛpʊpʊˈprɛy 'drizzle', wuwuˈkay 'cassava', awɛˈwɔi 'husband') and a few marks on the antepenult where a final glide+vowel sequence may or may not count as a syllable (ˈsɪksɪkɲɛy 'lightning', ˈuriki 'orphan'). My reading 'penultimate, with lexical exceptions' is an inference from token marks, not a statement of the source. Supporting machine count over the typed companions in the same folder (other entries, notes column only): MSS009 Babyotan 24 penult / 6 final / 4 other of 34 marked tokens; MSS011 Telalora 11/6/2 of 19; MSS013 Iblatmuntah 11/6/0 of 17; MSS002 Nura 5/2 of 7; MSS008 Lawawang 3/5 of 8; final-stressed typed tokens are mostly prefixed verbs with monosyllabic roots (nɛmˈkak, nɛˈtir, mɔˈpri, nɛˈrɔ).
new_statements.secondary_stress: none marked in the pages read (only primary ˈ and length ː appear)
new_statements.exceptions: none stated; observed final-stress tokens listed under rule_in_words (forms in -ɛy/-ay/-ɔi and prefixed verbs with monosyllabic roots)
new_statements.identity_note: The scans cover four West Marsela (mss) village varieties on Masela island, Kecamatan Pulau Masela, Kab. Maluku Barat Daya: Lawawang (1500-item list, speakers Tiwery family, 5-7 Aug 2025), Nura (315/481-item UBB list, 5 Aug 2025), Babyotan/Babiotan (8 Aug 2025) and Telalora (9 Aug 2025); the Iblatmuntah list named in the citation is not in hand as a scan (its typed version is). All recorded by Owen Edwards, ELAR IPF0417.

sources.note: Nothing on West Marsela (or any South Babar) word stress or tone. Phonological content about West Marsela is segmental/diachronic only: mid-high vs mid-low front vowel contrast (fn. 31), sound changes *s > t, *t > k, *k > 0, word-initial *a > u, *n > l with West Marsela examples (kun 'star', waky 'stone', muk 'eye', wal 'right', ul). The book's stress statements concern other languages (Kemak, Hawu/Dhao, Luang epenthetic schwa, Fordata/Yamdena/Kei, Seram languages). All 54 'stress' hits checked; none in the Babar section.
